elements.evidence: "IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY ... EXCEED"

elements.element: Cap limb (b): USD 1,000,000, expressed as the greater of the two limbs

elements.evidence: "NEITHER PARTY SHALL BE LIABLE FOR ANY INDIRECT OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES."

elements.element: Fallback: mutual cap of 12 months' fees
elements.evidence: "EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY ... EXCEED THE GREATER OF (A) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim" (fee limb present; preferred greater-of exceeds fallback floor)

elements.element: Fallback: carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct
elements.evidence: "CONFIDENTIALITY ... INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS, ITS GROSS NEGLIGENCE, WILLFUL MISCONDUCT"

reasons: All preferred atomic elements are present in operative text: a mutual, Agreement-wide cap at the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000, a mutual indirect/consequential exclusion, the full uncapped carve-out list (confidentiality, data protection, security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement), and an express statement that Client's payment obligations are not damages.

The official precision check on the payment-obligations element appears to be a false negative: the inserted sentence expressly says "Client's payment obligations, and all amounts due under this Agreement, are not damages for purposes of this limitation," which matches the position (and the broader "all amounts due" formulation the check itself contemplates).

Edits are surgical: one operator/number replacement in the existing cap sentence plus two short inserted sentences for the absent exclusion and carve-out mechanics; no unrelated term or untouched sentence is disturbed, and the Section 12(a) indemnity language is left intact.

Minor, non-flaggable residue: the original one-sided parenthetical "(OTHER THAN DUE TO A BREACH RESULTING FROM TRUELINK'S GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT)" survives and is now duplicated by the new mutual carve-out; it is harmless surplusage rather than a contradiction, but could be deleted for tidiness.

Note in the rationale (not as a deviation) that broadening the cap from Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11 to the whole Agreement was necessary to achieve mutuality; the carve-out sentence prevents that broadening from sheltering TrueLink's confidentiality, data, indemnity or misconduct exposure.
